question: Should OpenClaw adopt the remaining multi-charset Content-Disposition decoder as shared media-core behavior now, or keep the scope limited to the already-landed Feishu owner-path repairs while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48788 is decided?
rationale: Current main has already addressed the concrete Feishu JSON recovery path, but the branch adds broader decoding semantics at a shared media boundary; choosing that permanent scope is a product and ownership decision rather than a mechanical rebase.

options.title: Rebase and narrow to approved generic behavior
options.body: Recommended: rebase on current main, drop duplicated Feishu recovery, and retain only the generic decoder behavior maintainers explicitly want under the central tracker.

options.title: Pause for the centralization decision
options.body: Keep the branch open but do not merge until the owner of the central filename-decoding direction decides the supported charset and channel-boundary contract.

options.title: Close in favor of a fresh scoped PR
options.body: Close this stale conflicted branch and invite a smaller current-main PR after the canonical direction is chosen.

recommendation.title: Rebase and narrow to approved generic behavior
recommendation.body: Recommended: rebase on current main, drop duplicated Feishu recovery, and retain only the generic decoder behavior maintainers explicitly want under the central tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged Feishu recovery work is the closest established implementation and provides the clearest ownership context for avoiding a parallel path.
